text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.9% today as crude oil prices slid to $89.53 per barrel, their lowest level in this two-week period. The broader energy sector is under pressure: the epic run-up in refinery stocks is unwinding, and the collapse of international climate talks—which failed to address fossil fuels—has rattled investor confidence in oil companies' long-term prospects. The stock has now lost nearly 5% from its peak of $140.52 just a week ago.

Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, including Iran laying naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthis attacking Saudi refineries, have failed to prop up prices so far, suggesting markets are more focused on the softening demand picture than supply disruptions. The unwinding of the refinery trade—which had been a bright spot for energy stocks—signals that traders are rotating out of the sector more broadly.
